Need <x11/>neutral<x12/> (neutral cure), preferably electronics-grade.<x13/>2. <x14/>Hot glue.<x15/> Gun glue holds up to about 60-70°C, and on the playa, it's 45 in the shade and much more in the sun and black silicone. It will flow during operation — the cap will slide, dust and moisture will get inside.<x16/><x17/><x18/>Steps for each cut:<x19/> cut strictly on the mark (in WS2811 pixel — three diodes, cutting off-mark kills the whole group) → clean and tin contacts → solder wire → fill cap with neutral silicone and fit so silicone protrudes and seals the cut completely → let fully cure (neutral dries longer than acetic, up to a day) → only then test in operation.<x20/><x21/><x22/>What to glue with and why not with a gun.<x23/> Need a small tube at hand, not a cartridge for a gun: about 24 cuts, each a drop, and an open 300 ml tube will dry between sessions. The main thing is: <x30/>almost nothing sticks to silicone<x31/> — neither hot glue, nor epoxy, nor superglue. Silicone tube has such a surface that glue just peels off as a film. Dust 1-10 µm is stopped only by a final filter of class <x6/>MERV 13<x7/> (85-90% at 1-3 µm) or higher.
